theory.intro: The equations $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$ describe the path through the parameter $t$. Making $t$ the subject of the first and substituting it into the second links $x$ and $y$ directly.
facts: Eliminating $t$ gives the **Cartesian equation** $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}\cos^{2}\alpha}$, which contains no $t$.
Since $\sec^{2}\alpha=1+\tan^{2}\alpha$, the same path is also written $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\left(1+\tan^{2}\alpha\right)$.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ is negative, so the path is a parabola opening downwards.
The path only describes the flight, so its domain is $0\le x\le R$, where $R$ is the range.
Setting $y=0$ and taking the non-zero root gives the range $R$.
The gradient $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ gives the direction of motion at a point, through $\tan\phi=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.
At $x=0$ the gradient equals $\tan\alpha$, so it gives the angle of projection.
steps: Make $t$ the subject of the horizontal equation
State the domain of the path

foundation.question_text: A projectile launched from the origin has $x=20t$ and $y=25t-5t^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. Find the Cartesian equation of its path and state its domain.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Make $t$ the subject of the horizontal equation**
$t=\dfrac{x}{20}$
2. **Substitute into the vertical equation**
$y=25\left(\dfrac{x}{20}\right)-5\left(\dfrac{x}{20}\right)^{2}$
3. **Simplify to a quadratic in $x$**
$=\dfrac{5x}{4}-\dfrac{5x^{2}}{400}$
$=\dfrac{5x}{4}-\dfrac{x^{2}}{80}$
4. **State the domain of the path**
$y=0$ gives $x=0$ or $x=100$, so the path is $0\le x\le 100$.

foundation.question_text: A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=\dfrac{3}{2}x-\dfrac{1}{80}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. Find the range.
A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=\dfrac{1}{2}x-\dfrac{1}{160}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. Find the greatest height.
A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=\dfrac{5}{3}x-\dfrac{5}{216}x^{2}$. Find the angle of projection, to 1 d.p.
A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{5}{324}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. Find its height after it has travelled $12\text{ m}$ horizontally, to 1 d.p.

development.question_text: A projectile is launched from the origin with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, so that $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$. Show that $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$.
development.solution_text:
1. **Make $t$ the subject of the horizontal equation**
$t=\dfrac{x}{V\cos\alpha}$
2. **Substitute into the vertical equation**
$y=V\sin\alpha\left(\dfrac{x}{V\cos\alpha}\right)-\dfrac{1}{2}g\left(\dfrac{x}{V\cos\alpha}\right)^{2}$
3. **Simplify to a quadratic in $x$**
$=\dfrac{x\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}\cos^{2}\alpha}$
$=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$

development.question_text: An object is rolled horizontally off the top of a $20\text{ m}$ tower with initial velocity $5\underset{\sim}{i}$ metres per second. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the point of projection as the origin. Find the Cartesian equation of the path, and how far from the base of the tower the object lands.
development.solution_text:
$\dot{x}=5$ and $\dot{y}=-10t$
$x=5t$ and $y=-5t^{2}$
$t=\dfrac{x}{5}$
$y=-5\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{2}$
$=-\dfrac{x^{2}}{5}$
The ground is at $y=-20$.
$-20=-\dfrac{x^{2}}{5}$
$x^{2}=100$
$x=10$
The object lands $10\text{ m}$ from the base of the tower.

development.question_text: A projectile launched from the origin at speed $V$ and angle $\theta$ follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$. Show that the range is $\dfrac{V^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g}$, and hence find the two possible values of $\theta$, to 1 d.p., when $V=30\text{ m/s}$, $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the range is $75\text{ m}$.
A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{5}{324}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. Find the two horizontal distances at which its height is $19\text{ m}$, to 1 d.p.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{4}{3}x-\dfrac{5}{324}x^{2}=19$
Multiplying by $324$:
$432x-5x^{2}=6156$
$5x^{2}-432x+6156=0$
$x=\dfrac{432\pm\sqrt{186624-123120}}{10}$
$=\dfrac{432\pm 252}{10}$
$x=18$ or $x=68.4$
The height is $19\text{ m}$ at $18\text{ m}$ on the way up and at $68.4\text{ m}$ on the way down.

development.question_text: A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=2x-\dfrac{1}{50}x^{2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. Find the range, the greatest height, and the domain of the path.
development.solution_text:
$2x-\dfrac{1}{50}x^{2}=0$
$x\left(2-\dfrac{x}{50}\right)=0$
$x=0$ or $x=100$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2-\dfrac{x}{25}$
$2-\dfrac{x}{25}=0$
$x=50$
$y(50)=2(50)-\dfrac{1}{50}(50)^{2}$
$=100-50$
$=50$
The range is $100\text{ m}$, the greatest height is $50\text{ m}$, and the path is $0\le x\le 100$.

development.question_text: A ball is tossed from a point $O$ that is $6\text{ m}$ above the ground, at $24\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and $O$ as the origin. Show that the path is $y=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x-\dfrac{5}{432}x^{2}$, and find the horizontal distance travelled when the ball strikes the ground, to 1 d.p.
development.solution_text:
$\dot{x}=24\cos 30^{\circ}=12\sqrt{3}$ and $\dot{y}=-10t+12$
$x=12\sqrt{3}t$ and $y=-5t^{2}+12t$
$t=\dfrac{x}{12\sqrt{3}}$
$y=12\left(\dfrac{x}{12\sqrt{3}}\right)-5\left(\dfrac{x}{12\sqrt{3}}\right)^{2}$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x-\dfrac{5}{432}x^{2}$
The ground is at $y=-6$, so with $x=D$:
$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}D-\dfrac{5}{432}D^{2}=-6$
$5D^{2}-144\sqrt{3}D-2592=0$
$D=\dfrac{144\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{62208+51840}}{10}$
$\approx 58.7$
The ball lands $58.7\text{ m}$ horizontally from $O$.

mastery.question_text: A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$. It is launched at $V=20\text{ m/s}$ with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and passes through the point $(20,10)$. Show that $\tan^{2}\theta-4\tan\theta+3=0$, and hence find the two possible angles of projection, to 1 d.p.

A projectile launched from the origin follows $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\theta$. Show that its greatest height is $\dfrac{V^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$, and hence find $\theta$ when $V=20\text{ m/s}$, $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the greatest height is $15\text{ m}$.

A shell is fired from a gun at the origin with speed $V=200\text{ m/s}$ and elevation $\alpha$, taking $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the path $y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\sec^{2}\alpha$. Show that $gx^{2}\tan^{2}\alpha-2xV^{2}\tan\alpha+\left(2yV^{2}+gx^{2}\right)=0$, and hence find the two elevations that hit a target $3\text{ km}$ away horizontally and $0.5\text{ km}$ above the gun, to the nearest degree.
mastery.solution_text:
$y=x\tan\alpha-\dfrac{gx^{2}}{2V^{2}}\left(1+\tan^{2}\alpha\right)$
Multiplying by $2V^{2}$ and collecting terms:
$gx^{2}\tan^{2}\alpha-2xV^{2}\tan\alpha+\left(2yV^{2}+gx^{2}\right)=0$
With $x=3000$, $y=500$, $V=200$ and $g=10$:
$9\times 10^{7}\tan^{2}\alpha-2.4\times 10^{8}\tan\alpha+1.3\times 10^{8}=0$
$9\tan^{2}\alpha-24\tan\alpha+13=0$
$\tan\alpha=\dfrac{24\pm\sqrt{576-468}}{18}$
$=\dfrac{4\pm\sqrt{3}}{3}$
$\alpha\approx 62^{\circ}$ or $\alpha\approx 37^{\circ}$
